mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day forward period following any decline in FEDFUNDS (measured over the prior 3 months), the S&P 500 fails to produce positive returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment rate above 4.7% over 3 months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.7 for 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 3-month declines in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures indicate a broad-based demand contraction that reduces corporate revenue expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline for 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a 3-month decline in industrial production below its 6-month moving average signals weakening real economic activity, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, when INDPRO declines for 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in real personal consumption expenditures indicates strong consumer demand that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS rises for 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.5% for 3 consecutive months signals restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.5 for 3 months, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in industrial production below 100 indicates significant manufacturing slowdown that triggers recession expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100 for 3 months, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls for 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
